title: Subject-Verb Agreement
summary: How to make the verb match its subject, the tricky cases (each, everyone, neither...nor, one of, there is/are) and the agreement mistakes that lose marks every year.

blocks.text: The verb must **agree** with its subject: a **singular** subject takes a **singular** verb, and a **plural** subject takes a **plural** verb. First find the **subject** (who or what does the action), then choose the verb.

blocks.title: Past tense is easier
blocks.text: In the past simple, most verbs are the same for everyone: he played, they played. Only **be** changes: he **was**, they **were**.

rows: Singular subject → singular verb (+s in the present)
Two subjects joined by and → plural
either ... or / neither ... nor → the verb agrees with the **nearer** subject
Neither the teacher nor the students **were** ready. / Either the students or the teacher **is** coming.
everyone, everybody, someone, nobody, each, every → singular
Everyone **is** here. / Each child **has** a book.
The real subject, not the nearest noun
The box of chocolates **is** on the table. (the box is)
one of + plural noun → singular verb
One of my friends **lives** in Dubai.
There is + singular / There are + plural
There **is** a cat. / There **are** many shops.
Collective nouns (team, family, class) usually singular
Amounts of time, money and distance as one unit → singular
Ten kilometres **is** a long way to walk.

blocks.title: Find the real subject
blocks.text: Cover the words between the subject and the verb: The children **in the back row** are noisy. → The children are noisy. / The colour **of the flowers** is lovely. → The colour is lovely.
Words like **information, news, advice, furniture, homework, equipment, money, water** are uncountable. They always take a **singular** verb.
4. Mistakes the examiner sees every year

blocks.title: Watch out for these
items: there was many people ✗ → there were many people ✓
the information were ✗ → the information was ✓
my sister always forget ✗ → my sister always forgets ✓
one of the boys are ✗ → one of the boys is ✓

blocks.text: Agreement is mostly tested **in your writing**. It is part of **Grammar and punctuation** (7 marks): the examiner looks for sentences that are grammatically accurate. Small agreement errors like we was or there is many repeated through a piece can pull this mark down quickly.

blocks.title: In the reading section
items: You may be asked to **choose the correct verb** to complete a sentence, or to spot which sentence is grammatically correct.
Read every option **with the subject**: say the subject + verb together quietly in your head (Each of the girls ... has).

blocks.text: **When you proofread**, check every was/were, is/are, has/have and does/do. Ask: what is the subject? Is it one or more than one?

blocks.title: نصيحة سريعة
items: مع he و she و it والاسم المفرد: الفعل في المضارع ياخد s (she plays). ومع they والجمع: من غير s.
everyone و each و nobody مفرد دايمًا: Everyone is مش Everyone are.
There is للمفرد و There are للجمع. ما تقولش there was many people.

items.q: Choose: Neither my brother nor my sisters (like / likes) fish.
items.a: **like**: the verb agrees with the nearer subject, sisters (plural).

items.q: Choose: Each of the players (has / have) a shirt.
Correct: We was waiting at the gate for an hour.
items.a: We **were** waiting at the gate for an hour.

items.q: Choose: The basket of oranges (is / are) heavy.
items.a: **is**: the subject is the basket (singular), not oranges.

items.q: Correct: There is lots of cars in the street today.
items.a: There **are** lots of cars in the street today. (cars is plural)

items.q: Choose: Salma and her cousin (go / goes) swimming on Fridays.
items.a: **go**: two subjects joined by and are plural.

items.q: Correct: My dad don't like spicy food.
Choose: The news about the match (was / were) exciting.
items.a: **was**: news is uncountable, so it is singular.

items.q: Choose: One of the windows (is / are) broken.
items.a: **is**: one of takes a singular verb.

items.q: Choose: Everybody in my class (want / wants) a school trip.
